paragraphs.heading: Cold water below the surface
paragraphs.text: Deep ocean water is the name given to the cold, salty water of the deep sea. It starts 200 m (660 ft) down from the surface of the oceans on Earth. About 90% of all the water in the oceans, by volume, is deep ocean water. The term is typically used for water at depths great enough to give a measurable difference in water temperature.

paragraphs.heading: Temperature and salt
paragraphs.text: Ocean water is not the same everywhere, since it differs in temperature and in salinity. Warm water at the surface is generally saltier than the cooler water of the deep or of the polar regions. In polar regions the upper layers of the ocean are both cold and fresh. The temperature of deep ocean water is very uniform, at around 0–3 °C (32–37 °F). Its salinity is about 3.5%, which oceanographers state as 35‰, or parts per thousand.

paragraphs.heading: Pumping it up
paragraphs.text: In a few specialised places this water is brought to the surface. One is the Natural Energy Laboratory of Hawaii, where ocean water is pumped up from about 900 m (3,000 ft) deep. It is put to use there in research and in commercial and pre-commercial activities.

paragraphs.heading: Leftover cold
paragraphs.text: Cold ocean water may also have an indirect use. It comes from operations that use the water for condensation or for ocean thermal energy conversion. In these the water does not warm all the way to the temperature of its surroundings. That is because those processes need a certain temperature gradient to be viable, so the water that leaves them is still colder than the surroundings. More benefit can be drawn from it by running it through underground pipes, which cools agricultural soil.

paragraphs.heading: Farming with cold soil
paragraphs.text: Cooling the soil this way reduces evaporation, and it even makes water condense out of the atmosphere. That allows farming in places where crops would normally not be able to grow. The technique is sometimes called "cold agriculture" or "cold-bed agriculture".
